title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
event_hint: KAP (Knowledge Access Planning): a serving-time IR that compiles structured knowledge priors (e.g. GraphRAG) into a runtime access plan governing physical KV access, instantiated as GraphSpec on a vLLM backend.
problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: knowledge-selection frontends (RAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG) produce structured priors, but prompt serialization collapses them into a flat token stream, forcing the serving backend to densely consume the full KV state during decoding. Richer contexts enlarge the KV footprint and decode-time memory traffic, increasing latency and degrading throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of the context.
mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors into first-class physical execution artifacts via a universal IR - the runtime access plan - which compiles knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training. GraphSpec is a compiler-executor instantiation connecting a Graph-RAG frontend to a vLLM backend; it produces a selected-KV proposal view with full-context verification. A phase-boundary cost model characterizes the positive-speedup regime (margin h-s between acceptance rate h and retained-KV ratio s).

evidence.claim: Across 4K-128K long-context QA, GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K (10.8% at 64K, 40.1% at 4K) while maintaining answer quality comparable to full-context decoding.
evidence.condition: long-context QA, Graph-RAG frontend, vLLM backend
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 2; PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: GraphSpec improves decode throughput (TPS) over full-context baseline by 1.08x at 4K-16K, 1.09x at 32K, 1.13x at 64K, and 1.19x at 128K; speedup grows with context length as retained-KV ratio falls.

Answer quality is preserved: GraphSpec pass rate differs from full-context baseline by at most 0.3 percentage points at five of six lengths, and is 1.9 points higher at 64K; average similarity closely matched across 4K-128K (e.g., 0.741 vs 0.748 at 64K).
evidence.condition: LLM-as-judge pass rate at 0.5 threshold; independent human audit 95% agreement on 100 SPIQA samples
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 3; PDF Page 12 - Table 1

evidence.claim: Ablation (64K): Physical concat (same selected evidence materialized as shortened 0.95K prompt) pass rate falls to 73.9% vs 87.9% for GraphSpec; Random concat 49.7%, Local window 47.1%, confirming the runtime access plan - not prompt shortening - is the operative bridge.

Phase-boundary model consistency (RQ4): retained ratio s decreases from 0.401 (4K) to 0.055 (128K) while acceptance h stays high (0.953-0.962), so margin h-s grows from 0.557 to 0.897 and measured speedup rises from 1.08x to 1.19x without refitting the cost model.

evaluation_context: Long-context QA workloads (4K-128K tokens) with a Graph-RAG knowledge-selection frontend and vLLM serving backend. Quality metric: LLM-as-judge similarity in [0,1] with 0.5 pass threshold (4 dimensions: fact consistency 40%, information completeness 30%, logical structure 20%, expression quality 10%), independently audited against 3-annotator majority vote on 100 SPIQA samples (95% agreement). Efficiency metrics: decode throughput (TPS) and TTFT; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT (Graph-RAG evidence frozen before benchmarking). All serving-path measurements collected with diagnostic profiling disabled.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to one KAP instantiation (GraphSpec with Graph-RAG frontend + vLLM backend); authors explicitly state empirical evidence does not exhaust the broader design space. Results are strongest for long-context QA where graph-derived priors ground in evidence spans; effectiveness for other frontends, plan compilers, access policies, or backends is unverified. TTFT is slightly worse for GraphSpec at several lengths (e.g., 1.56s vs 1.51s at 4K) because plan compilation and selected-KV materialization are included. No production deployment scale, GPU hardware spec, or cost data is reported in the visible evidence.
project_relevance: KAP/GraphSpec is a serving-runtime/compiler optimization that reduces decode-time KV memory traffic by making structured knowledge priors executable - directly relevant to LLM serving efficiency and KV-cache management. It offers a concrete mechanism (runtime access plan IR) for decoupling physical KV consumption from prompt length. For the project card it is a research system evaluated on long-context QA, not a production deployment; its horizontal relevance is to inference serving rather than to the seven deep topics specifically.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.24260v1 (27 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from QiYuanLab.
Quality metric is LLM-as-judge (not human eval on all samples); independently audited on 100 SPIQA samples with 95% judge-human agreement.
Backend is vLLM; frontend is Graph-RAG; baselines are full-context vLLM, physical/random/local-window concat.
